entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "Limited Liability Company" or the abbreviation "L.L.C." or "LLC".
distinguishabilityNote: A domestic entity may not have a name that is the same as, or not distinguishable on the records of the Secretary of State from, the name of another existing filing entity or of a general partnership with an effective statement on file, the name of a foreign filing entity registered under Article 7, or a name already reserved. Entity-type designators (LLC, Inc., Corp., LP and the like) are not taken into account in that comparison unless the incumbent holder of the name waives that in writing, so a different ending alone does not make a name distinguishable. An indistinguishable name may still be used if the other entity or the holder of the reservation consents in writing and files an undertaking, in a form satisfactory to the Secretary of State, to change its own name to a distinguishable one. Alabama is also one of the few states where a name reservation is mandatory: a domestic LLC must obtain a Certificate of Name Reservation before it can file its Certificate of Formation, and it must attach that certificate to the formation document.
nameReservationCostBasis: The Secretary of State fee is $25 by paper and $28 online: the Name Reservation Request Form for Domestic Entities states a $25.00 processing fee by mail and says non-subscribers pay a $28 fee with a credit card to print the reservation immediately, and the fee schedule lists Name Reservations at $25.00. Because the reservation is a required step before formation, this is a mandatory cost for every domestic Alabama LLC, not an optional hold.
notes: Alabama's defining rule is the mandatory name reservation: unlike almost every other state, you cannot file LLC formation documents until the Secretary of State has issued a Certificate of Name Reservation for that exact name. The authority is § 10A-1-5.10 ("Mandatory Name Reservation for Certain Entities"), which also requires the certificate to be attached to the certificate of formation; the Secretary of State's LLC page still cites § 10A-1-4.02(f), but that subsection is about a filing officer returning an instrument it refuses to file. The application is made under § 10A-1-5.11 and the reservation runs for one year or until the applicant withdraws it (§ 10A-1-5.14), and it can be renewed. The Secretary of State's name reservation form adds agency clearances that are not in the statute: a banking entity needs a letter from the Alabama Banking Commissioner and an insurance entity a letter from the Alabama Insurance Commissioner (§ 10A-1-5.04(b) groups banks, trust companies, savings and loan associations and insurance companies together), and a name carrying a professional designation such as engineering, landscaping, architect, attorney or doctor needs an Alabama licence or a letter from the governing agency, with engineering and landscaping also needing a Certificate of Authorization from the Alabama Engineering Board. The flat bans on "bank," "trust," "insurance," "corporation" and "incorporated" in § 10A-1-5.05(e) apply to limited partnership names, not to LLCs. Alabama has no LLC annual report (it collects a separate Business Privilege Tax instead).
